content: Digoxin should only be taken if prescribed by a healthcare provider, and it must be used exactly as directed. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it could harm them. Always store digoxin out of the reach of children. Be aware that digoxin may impair your alertness or coordination, so avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring full attention until you understand how the medication affects you. Before starting digoxin, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, as well as any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This information will help your provider determine if digoxin is appropriate for you. Specifically, disclose if you have any of the following conditions: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, sinus node disease (sick sinus syndrome), atrioventricular (AV) block, kidney problems, myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle), heart failure with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, thyroid problems, chronic diarrhea, or a history of electrolyte imbalances (such as low potassium, magnesium, or calcium levels, or high calcium levels). If you are undergoing a medical procedure like electrical cardioversion, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking digoxin. Additionally, digoxin may interact with other medications and supplements, so provide your healthcare provider with a complete list of what you are taking. For more details, refer to the interactions section of the medication guide. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider, as it is not fully known how digoxin may affect pregnancy or an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether you should take digoxin during pregnancy. Similarly, if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, let your provider know, as digoxin passes into breast milk. The absorption of oral digoxin may be reduced if taken with meals high in bran fiber. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects digoxin, but drinking alcohol while on this medication may increase the risk of dizziness, blurred vision, and confusion. If you accidentally take too much digoxin, stop using the medication immediately and seek medical help. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Common side effects of digoxin include changes in heart rate or rhythm, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, blurry or yellow/green vision, headache, weakness, dizziness, confusion, anxiety, depression, hallucinations, enlarged breasts in men, and rash. If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, such as severe allergic reactions or significant changes in heart rate or rhythm, require immediate medical attention. Symptoms of a serious allergic reaction include difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, hives, or severe dizziness. Heart-related side effects, such as chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or irregular heartbeats, should also be reported immediately. Digoxin toxicity can occur if there is too much digoxin in your body. Symptoms include loss of appetite, persistent nausea or vomiting, diarrhea, confusion, weakness, vision changes, or abnormal heart rhythms. If you suspect digoxin toxicity, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Certain individuals should not use digoxin, including those allergic to digoxin, digitalis, Lanoxin, or any ingredients in the product. People with a type of abnormal heart rhythm called ventricular fibrillation should also avoid this medication. Always consult your pharmacist or healthcare provider for a complete list of ingredients in the specific digoxin product you are using. Finally, always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and do not use digoxin unless it has been prescribed for you.
